=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- CLAUDE.md: lines 925 and 927 (self-serve read list) vs lines 939-940 (Token hygiene) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §22.A authorizes sessions to self-serve read deployed app-level env vars ("verify that a name or value matches...") and build/deploy/runtime logs, both of which routinely contain consumer secrets (DB connection URLs, API keys, app tokens). The only redaction rule in §22.A ("Token hygiene") covers exclusively the DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN value, not any other secret material the session reads through this new path.
  WHY: An interactive session following the new policy can retrieve secret-bearing env var values or log lines and, with no rule requiring redaction beyond the DO token, may echo those secrets into its reply or the Claude session transcript, leaking a consumer's non-DO secrets.
- CLAUDE.md: line 986 ("§2 Q/A format, free-text answer allowed for the ID itself") vs line 67 ("Use stable identifiers Q1, Q2, etc. with letter-only answers (A, B, C, or A+C)") | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §22.C directs sessions to ask for a missing DigitalOcean resource ID using the §2 Q/A format while explicitly allowing a free-text answer. §2's Mandatory Question Format only defines multiple-choice, letter-only answers and one decision per Q-ID; it provides no mechanism for accepting an arbitrary free-form ID string.
  WHY: A session attempting to follow both rules has no valid format for the ask-for-ID flow: it must either violate §2's letter-only mandate or be unable to capture a free-form resource ID. The new policy's "ask once, then record the ID" workflow is inexpressible under the format it cites.
- changelog.d/digitalocean-token-access.md: filename (no issue-or-pr numeric prefix) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: §20.B requires changelog fragments to be named `changelog.d/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md`. This fragment is named without the issue-or-pr prefix. The assembler (`scripts/assemble_changelog.py`) globs every `*.md` and does not enforce the prefix, so there is no runtime failure, and some pre-existing fragments are also unnumbered.
  WHY: No runtime failure; this is non-compliance with the documented §20.B filename convention and weakens traceability to the owning issue/PR. Advisory only.
